annotation.reasoning_summary: Polygons represent housing association property areas/blocks as discrete real-world objects, not a tessellation or reporting units; the numeric fields are attributes, so ObjectDS.
Point features represent individual archaeological cesspits/find spots as discrete mapped objects, not measurements or events.
Point features mark individual archaeological finds/sites with object codes and descriptions; this is a set of mapped objects, not measurements or events.
Polygon features represent archaeological sites/vindplaatsen as discrete mapped objects, not a reporting unit or full-area coverage; ObjectDS fits the named site/object interpretation.

Polygon areas represent barbecue restriction/applicability zones in parks, so this is a bounded patch rather than a tessellation or object; the decisive rule is PatchDS for zones where a condition applies.
Polygons are conservation areas rather than reporting units or full tessellations; the decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded protected zones where a preservation condition applies.
Point features with observed bee records; the year field shows occurrence/observation timing, so this is best treated as event-like observations at points.
Point layer where the mapped phenomenon is the numeric amount of honey bee colonies/hives at each location, so PointDS + AmountDS.

Polygon layer of soil-quality zones/areas with reporting-unit terms like gebiednummer, zone, and statistische kentallen; the regions function as statistical/reporting units, so VectorTessellation + LatticeDS.
Points represent individual trees as identifiable objects; numeric fields are attributes of each tree, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point layer of individual trees; each point represents a distinct real-world object rather than a measurement or event, so PointDS + ObjectDS.
Point features are individual trees, and the main phenomenon is the mapped tree object/species rather than a measurement or amount.
Points represent individual trees, which are discrete mapped objects; numeric fields like height, year, and radius are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point features map neighborhood compost sites as identifiable places/facilities; numeric attributes are just site details, not the main phenomenon.
Polygons are selected camera areas tied to overlast/monitoring zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units; by the patch rule these are bounded applicability/phenomenon areas.
Point features represent individual trees (Canadian poplars); the layer maps distinct objects, not measurements or events.
Point features represent individual crowd-monitoring sensors/cameras, i.e. discrete real-world objects; the numeric fields are just attributes, so this follows the point-object rule.
Polygon areas represent named cultural-historical exploration sites/areas, not a full tessellation or reporting units; the mapped feature is the bounded object/place itself.
Point features map knotweed occurrences/infested locations; each point is a distinct observed object/location, not a measurement layer or event.

Point geometry with each feature representing a distinct ecopassage-related object/location (knelpunt, bridge, passage, or related asset), so the decisive rule is PointDS + ObjectDS rather than amount or event.
Polygon areas represent potential wind-energy areas, i.e. bounded phenomenon zones rather than a tessellation or discrete objects; numeric MW/GWh are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point features represent polling/stem locations as discrete places; the election totals and percentages are attributes of those locations, so this is ObjectDS rather than AmountDS.
Point features represent individual trees/nesting locations for oak processionary caterpillar nests; the mapped thing is the object itself, not a measurement or event.
Polygon areas mark pedicab permission/restriction zones, so this is a bounded applicability area rather than objects or a tessellation.
Point features mark fixed standplaatsen (pitches) for pedicabs/koetsen, so the mapped thing is the facility/object rather than a measurement or event.
Point features represent non-residential address-level functions; the mapped thing is each facility/place object, not a measurement or event.
Polygons form a near-complete partition of blocks/streets, and the layer is a full-area functional classification (WON/VZN/WRK mix), so VectorTessellation + CoverageDS.
Neighborhood boundary polygons form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, and the layer is a reporting-unit geography ('Wijken' / buurtcombinaties), so tessellation + lattice.
Neighborhood/combinatie polygons form a reporting-unit tessellation; the layer maps administrative/statistical areas with area attributes, so LatticeDS.
Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete area partition, and the layer is a reporting-unit administrative geography (buurten/stadsdeel), so VectorTessellation + LatticeDS.
Neighborhoods are reporting/statistical units that partition the area, so this is a tessellation and a lattice.
City districts are administrative/reporting units that partition the area, so geometry is a tessellation and the entity is LatticeDS.
Administrative city-district reporting units forming a near-complete partition; classified as VectorTessellation and LatticeDS.
Administrative/reporting areas (‘Gebieden’, ‘stadsdeel’) that partition the city, so the layer is a tessellation of reporting units rather than patches or objects.
Administrative area set of 22 gebieden forming a partition-like regional layer; treated as reporting units (gebied/stadsdeel) rather than objects or patches.

Polygon regions appear to be practice-area reporting units that partition Amsterdam; Stadsdeel_code and area fields support the reporting-unit rule, so geometry is a tessellation and entity is LatticeDS.
These are practice-area polygons that partition the city area, so geometry is tessellation. The layer is a set of named area/reporting units with district codes and area values, which fits LatticeDS.
Noise contours are isoline/interval bands shown as polygons, so the geometry is region-based and the entity is ContourDS.
Polygon isolines/interval bands for aircraft noise levels (55-60, 60-65, etc.); geometry is non-tessellating regions and the decisive rule is contour/value-band representation.
The layer is about noise contour bands (50-55 dB, 55-60 dB, etc.), so the decisive rule is contour/isoline representation rather than object or reporting-unit mapping.
Polygon noise contour bands with dB classes indicate isoline/interval contour zones rather than objects or reporting units.
Point features represent polling/stem locaties (voting stations) with election results as attributes, so geometry is PointDS and the mapped thing is the station/object rather than the numeric totals.
Point features map individual green roof sites at specific addresses; the mapped thing is each roof/object, not a measurement or event.
Land use 2017 is an area-wide thematic classification with polygons that partition the study area, so it fits tessellation geometry and coverage entity.
Point layer of distinct historical buildings and structures; the points represent identifiable objects, not measurements or events.

Polygon features are three bounded areas, not a tessellation or reporting units. The layer title and geometry indicate discrete municipal-area objects; the numeric ID is just an attribute, so ObjectDS.
Polygons represent dog off-leash and ban zones, i.e. bounded restriction/phenomenon areas rather than objects; this fits PatchDS and non-tessellated region geometry.
Polygons are discrete green-structure areas rather than a full tessellation, and the layer maps green-zone extents/types (patch) rather than reporting units or a numeric amount.
Point features represent individual elm trees as identifiable objects, with species and tree attributes as fields; this is an object layer, not a point-measurement or amount layer.
Point features represent discrete housing projects/buildings; the main mapped thing is the housing object itself, not a measured amount. Numeric dwelling counts are attributes, so ObjectDS.
Point features represent individual chestnut trees/locations; the layer maps identifiable objects with condition attributes, not measurements or events.
Point locations sample a continuous climate/hydrology field; the main mapped phenomenon is measured values at points, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.
Polygon areas represent flood-risk zones classified by probability and depth; this is a bounded phenomenon extent, so PatchDS. The regions are not a full tessellation or reporting units.
Point locations represent individual markets as identifiable places/facilities, not measurements or events; the decisive rule is point objects -> ObjectDS.
Point features represent named green monuments/parks/plantsoenen as discrete protected objects, not measurements or events.
Point features represent individual monumental trees; the layer maps discrete objects, not measurements or events.
Points indicate discrete locations, and the layer maps monuments as identifiable real-world objects/assets rather than measurements or events.
Point features map individual plant occurrences/species at quay walls; the main phenomenon is distinct biological objects, not measurements or events.
Polygon regions map NO2 measurement values over 4-week periods; this is a numeric magnitude layer, not reporting units or objects, so AmountDS.
Point locations for NO2 measurements; the main phenomenon is sampled measurement values at stations/locations, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.
Polygon regions that appear to mark selected gulch/phenomenon areas rather than a full tessellation or reporting units; best fit is PatchDS based on bounded area extent.
Points represent sounding locations with measured subsurface values (e.g., Top_Pleistoceen, depths), so this is a point measurement layer.
Polygon regions are named development neighbourhoods/wards used as reporting or planning units, so the layer is a tessellation of administrative-style units (LatticeDS).
Point features represent individual public toilet facilities, so the geometry is PointDS and the mapped thing is a discrete object/facility, not an amount or event.
Polygon neighborhoods/buurt units used as reporting units for overnight policy rules, so the geometry is a tessellation and the entity is LatticeDS.
Polygon areas show parking standards zones rather than full tessellation or named objects; this fits PatchDS, with PlainVectorRegion because the polygons do not form a complete partition.

Polygons map named parks/green spaces as discrete bounded places, so this is ObjectDS rather than a reporting unit or patch; geometry is PlainVectorRegion because the areas do not form a full tessellation.
Postcode4-buurten are postcode-based reporting units that partition the area, so this is a tessellation with lattice/reporting-unit meaning.
Postal code neighbourhood polygons form a near-complete partition, so geometry is tessellation; postcode areas are reporting units, so entity is LatticeDS.
Postcode6-vlakken are postcode reporting units that partition the area, so this is a tessellation and a lattice/reporting-unit layer.
LineString layer of plus and main transport infrastructure; the decisive rule is NetworkDS for connected route/system lines.
Line-system layer about plus networks/pedestrian network areas, so the decisive rule is NetworkDS; polygons are discrete mapped regions rather than a tessellation.
Point features named as specific masts/locations; the layer maps identifiable objects, not measurements or events.
Point features representing privacy-related research/analysis entries; the main meaning is an occurrence/activity (event), not a place or measurement.
Point features represent named scan locations/roadside sites with addresses; this is an object layer, not measurements or events.
Point layer of election reporting units/polling locations; the mapped features are district-based reporting units with vote totals, so Geometry is PointDS and Entity is LatticeDS.
Polygon layer over named buurten/gebieden used to attach drainage possible/not possible status, so it fits reporting units; polygons also act as a tessellation.

Polygon areas represent Rainproof hydro units, i.e. selected solution/issue areas where flood-related measures apply; not a full tessellation or reporting-unit lattice. PatchDS fits the bounded phenomenon zones.
Polygons mark rainproof bottleneck areas where water accumulation applies, not a full reporting tessellation or discrete object; this fits a selected phenomenon patch.
Polygon regions are selected Rainproof sewerage areas, not a full tessellation or reporting units; the decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded zones where the phenomenon/policy applies.
Point features represent identifiable religious buildings/locations with names and addresses, so this is PointDS + ObjectDS rather than a measurement or event layer.
Line geometries represent sidewalk segments in a street network; the layer is about connected pedestrian infrastructure, not a point/area measure.
LineString features describe road segments/routes for mopeds on the roadway, so this is a connected transport network.
Points map distinct public sports facilities/playgrounds; the layer is about identifiable objects, not measurements or events.
Point geometry with each feature representing a distinct city-farming location/site (named garden, farm, school garden, or project), so ObjectDS is the best fit.
Polygon features are discrete city-farming terrains with names, addresses, and websites, so they are mapped objects rather than a full tessellation or a patch zone.
Point features represent named initiatives/activities (objects or places), not measurements or events; no network or patch semantics are indicated.
LineString features map major streets; the decisive rule is the connected transport/street system, so NetworkDS with LineDS geometry.
LineString features map a transport network for district heating/cooling, so the decisive rule is network/route system.
Polygon layer named as wijk/neighbourhood; regions function as reporting units for district heating/cooling status, so VectorTessellation with LatticeDS.
Polygon areas map strategic housing-plan zones/areas of opportunity, not a full tessellation or reporting units; the decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded planning areas.
Point features represent distinct local farming businesses/places with names, addresses, products, and hours, so this is PointDS with ObjectDS rather than a measurement or amount layer.
LineString features represent tram and metro routes; the decisive rule is network/route system.
LineString features represent tram and metro route infrastructure, so the decisive rule is network/route system.
Point features represent tram stops and metro stations; the main phenomenon is a transport network of stops/stations served by lines, so NetworkDS.
Point features represent tram stops and metro stations; this is a set of identifiable transit objects, not a measurement or event layer.
Point layer of traffic lights at intersections; each point is a distinct mapped object, not a measurement or event.
Line geometry with road links; traffic prognosis values (etmaal and modal flows) are the main mapped phenomenon on each link, so this is a line amount layer rather than a pure network layer.

Point features are polling locations/stemlocaties, and the layer maps an election result tied to an event in time (Tweede Kamer 2017); numeric vote fields are attributes of those event-linked places, not the main phenomenon.
Points represent individual trees as identifiable objects; attributes like species, planting year, diameter, and height are object properties, not the main mapped quantity.
Point features represent individual traffic information system assets (cameras, signs, displays) at standplaatsen; this is a mapped object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features represent individual traffic information system installations/equipment (BFA objects), not measurements or events; numeric fields are just attributes, so ObjectDS.
Point features map breeding bird observations over years at locations, so the decisive rule is point geometry with an occurrence/event-style layer rather than objects or amounts.
Point features represent individual benches, a countable real-world asset/object; numeric rotation is just an attribute, not the main mapped phenomenon.
LineString street-segment features map walkability classes and related intensity categories; this is a linear thematic field rather than objects or a network.
Point features map individual wall-art works at specific locations; the layer is about identifiable artworks/objects, not measurements or events.
Polygon areas represent welstandniveau zones/restriction-applicability areas for buildings, not a full tessellation or discrete objects; patch rule fits better than object or coverage.
Polygon regions represent area-wide urban typology/system classes ('Welstandsystemen') rather than discrete objects or selected patches, so this fits CoverageDS with plain regional geometry.
Point features map WWII incidents/attacks at addresses with dates; this follows the event rule for points.
Polygons represent discrete housing development projects/phases with project names and dwellings counts, so ObjectDS fits better than patch or lattice; the areas are not a full tessellation.
Point features map discrete self-build plots/projects as identifiable places/assets, not measurements or events; numeric fields are just attributes, so ObjectDS.
Polygons represent individual roof/heritage-related objects with category labels, not a full tessellation or reporting units; best fits ObjectDS.
Point features represent solar panel installations; numeric fields are attributes of those objects, so this is ObjectDS rather than AmountDS.
Point features mark named swimming locations and facilities (bathing spots, pools, beaches), so this is PointDS with ObjectDS.
